solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grim days with British gone: such a loss!

indicators.note: gone after the British letter means that letter is taken away from the words before it

parts.note: grim means bleak
days, as in an era, means age

explanation.surface: A lament over hard times since Britain left: what a loss!
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is a loss of fluid, money or information that escapes, so it is exactly such a loss.

clue.text: Camilla did appear a little snooty

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Queen Camilla came across as somewhat stuck-up.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da mocks a pretentious, affected manner, the same as snooty.

clue.text: Setter's existence? It's not much fun

definitions.meaning: a setter is a breed of dog, so its existence is literally ...
... is an idiom for a miserable existence

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter grumbles that their life is no fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a hard, wretched existence, while a setter is literally a gun dog.

clue.text: Lover needing protection runs away

indicators.note: runs away means the runs letter goes from the word for protection

parts.note: armour is protection
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lover needing to be shielded flees.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is French for love, and in English means a love affair or a lover.

clue.text: Chap from the orient giving E to head of state?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern, read out in full
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: A man from the east handing the letter E to a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the single letter E is read in full as the word it abbreviates, and 'giving ... to' sets it before the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The orient is the east, so a man from there is an easterner.

clue.text: Hit the roof, bath covered in blood

indicators.note: covered in says one piece sits wrapped inside the other

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a spa is a bath or mineral spring, as in the town of Bath

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: someone struck on the roof, the bath smeared with blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To go spare is British slang for losing your temper, the same idiom as hitting the roof.

clue.text: Reportedly took a stab at visitor

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: to take a stab at something is to guess

explanation.surface: A visitor was reportedly attacked with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took a stab at' suggests a knife attack but means attempted an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person invited to visit.

clue.text: Late aunts perished in Muslim land

indicators.note: perished means fallen apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Dead aunts who died in an Islamic country.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate is a state ruled by a sultan, a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: A party engendering shame

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A party causing someone embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or embarrassed.

clue.text: Moderation at an end — 100 banished

indicators.note: banished means sent away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: something ceasing is coming to an end
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Moderation finishes once a hundred people are expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing is a lessening or relaxing, a moderation of pressure.

clue.text: Old married couple sitting outside cathedral

indicators.note: sitting outside says the couple goes round the other letters

parts.note: a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: An elderly married pair sit outside a cathedral, perhaps on an Italian holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Duomo is the Italian word for a cathedral, used in English for those of Florence and Milan.

clue.text: Successful slimmers do this a lot

definitions.meaning: people who slim successfully ... of weight
informal British for a great deal

explanation.surface: Dieters who succeed do this in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedloads is slang for a large amount, while slimmers literally lose a great deal of weight.

clue.text: New editor's in muddle

indicators.note: new says these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly appointed editor finds the office in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the editor but is the anagram signal on EDITORSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorient someone is to confuse them, the verb sense of muddle.

clue.text: Very pale, like bride-to-be

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as white as snow'
a hen is a bride-to-be, from the British hen party (bachelorette party)

explanation.surface: Pale as a nervous bride before her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey like ash.

clue.text: FBI troubled by last of Boris's deceptions

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed into a new order
last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The FBI rattled by the lies of a politician called Boris.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibs are small lies, a casual word for deceptions.

clue.text: A foregone conclusion? Absolutely

explanation.surface: Asked if the result is decided, someone says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sure thing is a certainty, and as a reply it means of course.

clue.text: Singer, half-naked with unruly hair

indicators.note: half- keeps only the front half of the word it is fixed to

parts.note: naked means nude
a thatch is a thick untidy head of hair

explanation.surface: A half-dressed figure with messy hair, perhaps a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird here, not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird, and crosswords often call any bird a singer.

clue.text: Discussion of psychotherapy perhaps

definitions.meaning: a ... of a subject is a discussion of it
psychotherapy is an example of medical ...

explanation.surface: A talk about therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment means how a topic is handled in writing, and also care given to a patient.

clue.text: Coercing European to become a caretaker

indicators.note: to become says these letters turn into another word

explanation.surface: Pushing a European into taking a caretaking job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges COERCING, and E for European follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge looks after a building, like a caretaker or porter.

clue.text: Where you might find A. Partridge?

definitions.text: Where you might find A. Partridge?

parts.words: Where you might find A. Partridge?
parts.note: the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' puts a partridge in this tree, and A. Partridge reads like the TV character Alan Partridge

explanation.walkthrough: 'A. Partridge' looks like Alan Partridge, a British TV comedy character, but split as 'a partridge' it recalls the Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first gift is a partridge perched in a fruit tree of this kind.

clue.text: Bet knocked back? I'm fuming!

indicators.note: knocked back sends the word for a bet in the opposite direction

parts.note: an ante is a stake or bet in poker

explanation.surface: Someone whose wager is refused explodes with anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, and a volcano might say it is fuming as it smokes.

clue.text: A sailor's two wrongs

parts.note: the first of the two wrongs: a sin is a moral wrong
the second of the two wrongs: bad is wrong as a noun, as in doing bad

explanation.surface: A seaman's two misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two wrongs' asks for two words meaning wrong, written one after the other; the 's after sailor is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the sailor of the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Heartbroken Yank embracing Masai woman?

indicators.note: embracing says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A grieving American hugging a woman from East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a people of Kenya, so a Masai woman is an example of a Kenyan.

clue.text: Pub has attractive quality, don't you think?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it is sex appeal, as in an 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pub's charm, seeking agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is slangy British for 'isn't it?', a tag asking agreement.

clue.text: Opera that's just like the others? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: normal means typical, just like the others

explanation.surface: A critic says an opera is nearly but not quite run-of-the-mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is an opera by Bellini.

clue.text: Commission writer one sees occasionally

parts.note: an author is a writer
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: occasionally takes only every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer on commission sees someone only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission work is to authorise or empower someone to carry it out.

clue.text: Modify Moscow agreement in right context

indicators.note: in says the agreement is placed inside the other word
context is the setting that surrounds the agreement

parts.note: apt means right or fitting
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: Changing a Russian deal to suit the right circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to adjust or change something for a new use.

clue.text: Dull job shifting old paint

indicators.note: shifting says one letter is moved to a new spot in the word

parts.note: a chore is a dull task

explanation.surface: Stripping old paint is a tedious task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' moves the O of CHORE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used in paint.

clue.text: Arab cried pitifully in bar

indicators.note: pitifully means badly or wretchedly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Arab man wept pitifully in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a drinking place but is a verb or noun meaning obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier, and to bar a way is to barricade it.

clue.text: Hound a chap of royal blood

definitions.meaning: Prince ... is a man of the British royal family

explanation.surface: Hounding a royal man, as the tabloids do.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry means persistently harass, and is also the name of a British prince.

clue.text: Drink? Doctor will have anything

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A doctor offers anything to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single swallow of liquid, so a drink.

clue.text: Neither will dance in that place

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Neither partner will dance at that venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is formal English for inside that, or in that place.
